'''''Cyclamen repandum''''', the '''spring sowbread''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007|accessdate=2014-10-17}}</ref> is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] Primulaceae, [[native plant|native]] to southern Europe and some Mediterranean islands. It is the most widespread of a group of cyclamens ([[genus]] ''[[Cyclamen]]'' subgenus ''[[Cyclamen#Subgenus Psilanthum|Psilanthum]]'') with wide, heart-shaped [[leaf|leaves]], often coarsely toothed or lobed, and late spring-blooming [[flower]]s with long, slender [[petal]]s.

==Etymology==
The name of the subgenus, ''Psilanthum'', comes from [[Ancient Greek]] {{Lang|grc-Latn|psilós}} "bare" and {{Lang|grc-Latn|ánthos}} "flower".<ref>{{LSJ|yilo/s|ψιλός}}, {{LSJ|a)/nqos1|ἄνθος<sup>1</sup>|ref}}</ref> The species name ''repandum'' is [[Latin]] for "bent back" or "turned up".<ref>{{L&S|repandus|rĕpandus|ref}}</ref>

==Description==
''Cyclamen repandum'' grows in [[rock (geology)|rocky]] areas, [[shrubland]], and [[woodland]] near the Mediterranean from southeastern France through Italy to Serbia and on Corsica, Sardinia, and Sicily. The [[tuber]] of the ''C. repandum'' group roots only from the center of the bottom. Leaves are dark green with a lighter arrowhead pattern, not speckled. [[Flower]]s are deep carmine-pink or white, without a darker nose. They lack the [[auricle (botany)|auricles]] present in ''[[Cyclamen hederifolium]]''.

==Similar species==
The ''Cyclamen repandum'' group also includes ''[[Cyclamen rhodium|C. rhodium]]'', ''[[Cyclamen balearicum|C. balearicum]]'', and ''[[Cyclamen creticum|C. creticum]]''.

==Hybrids==
When species of the ''Cyclamen repandum'' group are growing together, [[Hybrid (biology)#Hybrid plants|hybrids]] can emerge:
*''Cyclamen'' × ''meiklei'' <small>Grey-Wilson</small> (''C. creticum'' × ''C. repandum'')
*''Cyclamen'' × ''saundersii'' <small>Grey-Wilson</small> (''C. repandium'' × ''C. balearicum'')
*''Cyclamen creticum'' × ''Cyclamen balearicum''

== Cultivation ==
''Cyclamen repandum'' is a [[deciduous]] plant that has a hardiness rating of H4<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/trials-awards/award-of-garden-merit/rhs-hardiness-rating|title=Check how hardy plants are using RHS hardiness ratings / RHS Gardening|website=www.rhs.org.uk|access-date=2020-02-22}}</ref> (This refers to the UK growing conditions, H4 being hardy through most of the UK and can withstand temperatures down to {{Convert|-5 to -10|C}}). It requires partial shade and can grow in [[chalk]], [[clay]], [[sand]] or [[loam]]. It can grow in any [[PH|pH level]]; [[acid]], [[Alkali|alkaline]] or neutral. ''C. repandum'' can grow to an ultimate height of {{Convert|10|cm|abbr=on}} and can take anywhere between 2–5 years to reach this height.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/5155/i-Cyclamen-repandum-i/Details|title=Cyclamen repandum|last=|first=|date=2020|website=Royal Horticultural Society|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190629150947/https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/5155/i-Cyclamen-repandum-i/Details |archive-date=2019-06-29 |access-date=22 February 2020}}</ref>

The [[subspecies]] ''C. repandum'' subsp. ''repandum'' (wavy-edged cyclamen) has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]]<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Cyclamen repandum'' subsp. ''repandum''|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/106107/Cyclamen-repandum-subsp-repandum/Details | accessdate=19 February 2020}}</ref> (confirmed 2017).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf|title=AGM Plants - Ornamental|date=July 2017|page=26|publisher=Royal Horticultural Society|accessdate=24 January 2018}}</ref>
